title: SSO failover triggered signed-audit digest mismatch and ingestion drop; remediation plan
creator: Aisha Raman
description: During an automated SSO provider failover window we observed a small window (~18 minutes) of dropped audit ingestion resulting from a signed-digest verification mismatch between the auth proxy and the audit-ingest verifier. The mismatch occurred because a short-lived token re-issuance path used a legacy signing key reference while a KMS rotation was in progress for the audit signer; the auth proxy signed entries with a rotated key alias while the ingest verifier was still validating against the previous key fingerprint. Missing entries impacted auth-related audit trails for several customer tenants in us-west-2 and caused compliance alerts. This ticket tracks the post-incident remediation, reconciliation of missing entries, and long-term fixes to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-01T02:04:12Z - SSO provider initiated failover; auth proxy began re-issuing tokens using the local signing library
2026-03-01T02:06:30Z - KMS key rotation job for audit-signer started (scheduled rotation), rotated alias propagated to some auth proxy hosts
2026-03-01T02:15:05Z - Audit-ingest verifier experienced digest validation failures; ingestion queue grew and several entries were dropped by verifier policy

2026-03-01T02:22:00Z - On-call SRE paged; initial mitigation applied (fallback to unsigned ingest path and temporary allowlist for affected tenants), mitigation increased ingestion latency but stopped further drops
2026-03-01T02:30:45Z - Temporary hotfix deployed: auth proxy forced to use canonical key alias and ingestion verifier refreshed key cache; reconstruction of dropped entries started
root_cause: Race between SSO failover token re-issuance path and scheduled KMS rotation leading to inconsistent key alias usage across auth proxy and audit-ingest verifier. The verifier's key-cache TTL and rotation propagation monitoring were insufficient to guarantee atomic key transitions across clustered services during provider failovers.
mitigation: Immediate: Rolled back auth proxy to canonical signing alias on all affected hosts
Immediate: Temporarily enabled a permissive ingest path to avoid permanent loss of customer-visible audit events while retaining evidence in staging queues
Immediate: Triggered manual key-cache refresh on ingestion fleet and increased log-levels for digest verification to collect diagnostics
Short term: Replayed buffered audit events from staging with re-signed digests after canonical key re-association to ensure audit trails are complete
long_term_actions: (Owner: Diego) Implement atomic rotation protocol: coordinator that sequences KMS alias swap + global key-cache refresh hook so verifier and signers update in a single window — target Q2 2026
(Owner: Priya Shah) Add pre-rotation compatibility checks and simulated failover run in staging to validate signer/verifier behavior during SSO failovers — due 2026-04-15
(Owner: SRE) Reduce key-cache TTL for audit-ingest verifier and add jittered refresh on error to avoid stale verification state — due 2026-03-21
(Owner: Security) Update runbook: on SSO provider failover during rotation, pause rotation and run cross-service key verification checklist — due 2026-03-18
(Owner: Eng Tools) Build an audit-replay tool to rehydrate dropped entries and annotate replays for downstream compliance report generation — due 2026-04-01
reconstruction_plan: We will reconcile by reprocessing buffered auth event batches from staging with canonical key re-signing where possible. For entries that cannot be re-signed (external third-party signed tokens), we will mark them in a compliance reconciliation report with original timestamps and include HMAC fingerprints captured by proxy logs. Expected completion: 2026-03-22.
validation_criteria: Zero digest verification failures for 72 hours across a simulated SSO failover matrix in staging
Key alias convergence time across signer and verifier clusters < 30s in synthetic tests
Automated smoke test that simulates token re-issuance + KMS rotation completes without dropped audit records
Compliance team sign-off on reconciliation report and replayed audit integrity verification
